articleTitle: Analysis and Evaluation Performance of MPPT Algorithms: Perturb & Observe (P&O), Firefly, and Flower Pollination (FPA) in Smart Microgrid Solar Panel Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: There are various factors that can affect the performance quality of solar panel systems, one of them is the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithms. The AI algorithm can be used in switching converter control systems to achieve the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) position from the power characteristic curve of solar panel voltage. The use of an appropriate AI algorithm will support tracking quality or assessment of the duty cycle. Changes in the value of the duty cycle will affect the solar power output value of the solar panel. Tracking the accurate duty cycle will produce the most optimal output of solar power. To support system performance, the algorithm used as MPPT must have a short tracking rate or convergence time. To find out which algorithm is the best, a comparison is made by simulating a solar panel system which is then connected to a smart microgrid network. Testing of solar panel systems is carried out under varying irradiation conditions. In this study, simulations were carried out with several different algorithms to produce maximum power values. Based on the results of the test, it can be concluded that the FPA algorithm is considered the most optimal with the largest output power of 140.81 watts. In addition, the FPA algorithm also succeeded in becoming the fastest method of finding power with a maximum time of 0.02 seconds. The final results of the study can be used to support the improvement in the quality of performance of the smart microgrid solar panel system.

articleTitle: Towards 100% renewable electricity for Indonesia: the role for solar and pumped hydro storage
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: 60% of global annual net new capacity comprise the addition of solar photovoltaics (PV) and wind. Indonesia has good solar resources by world standards, with low seasonal variation. There is also some wind energy potential. Solar PV is likely to be cheaper than new coal generation and can be rapidly deployed at every scale throughout Indonesia. Balancing an electricity system with large fractions of variable solar PV and wind can be managed with established techniques comprising stronger interconnection over large areas to average out local weather variations; storage; demand management; and occasional spillage of renewable electricity. Pumped hydro is by far the leading method of energy storage. Indonesia has 26,000 good pumped hydro sites with storage capacity of 821,000 Gigawatt-hours (GWh), which is about 1,000 times more than needed to support a 100% renewable Indonesian electricity system.

articleTitle: Analysis of Voltage and Power Factor Fluctuation due to Photovoltaic Generation in Distribution System Model
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) to the system is aimed to reduce CO2 emissions and the needs of fossil fuels power plant in the future. In the last ten years, globally photovoltaic (PV) generation growth exponentially. This is because the trend of PV generation installation cost is decreasing and the cost of energy source is free of charge. In Indonesia, it's predicted the price of energy per kWhp generated by the PV system will reach the parity system by 2028. Mass usage of the rooftop PV system will speed up this process. The rapid growth of the PV generation will have a big impact on voltage regulation in distribution networks, especially at lower voltage levels due to more significant intermittent irradiance effects. The analysis was carried out using power system analysis software on a uniformly distributed distribution system model using real recorded consumers load and PV generation. The simulation will focus on the magnitude of voltage rise or voltage drop in the distribution system, where is described relative to the percentage of penetration and the installation location of PV. Several penetration scenarios are analyzed to get a comprehensive result on the voltage fluctuation magnitude by high, moderate, and low penetration level. There is more fluctuation value of power factor (PF) which is caused by higher penetration of rooftop PV. The installation of the PV generation close to the transformer gives better voltage fluctuation.

articleTitle: Predicting Rooftop Photovoltaic Adoption In The Residential Consumers of PLN Using Agent-Based Modeling
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Indonesia has a massive solar energy potential of about 207 gigawatts in 2015, unfortunately, the utilization only 0.04 percent. In 2017, the rooftop photovoltaic (PV) in Indonesia has become a trend adopted by residential consumers. Increasing the adoption of rooftop PV is one of the strategies to reach the 23 percent renewable energy mix by 2025. Therefore, to predict the rooftop PV adoptions in the future, Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) is applied. The purpose of the model is to understand the impact of decision-making behavior for the adoption of rooftop PV at the household level on electricity utilization from PLN. The simulation results are divided into sensitivity analysis and scenario analysis.The analysis indicates that the factors inherent in consumer behavior such as the level of adoption to adopt new technologies, the number of neighbors who have installed rooftop PV, lifestyle and intensity of exposure to social media have influenced the rate of adoption. The simulation results of several sensitivity analyses show that the higher the ability of households to adopt new technologies and increased the number of neighbors who have installed rooftop PV have an impact on the increasing level of adoption on rooftop PV in this community. Meanwhile, the results of the scenario analysis showed that decreasing the price of rooftop PV per year and increased government subsidies have an impact on the increasing adoption rate of rooftop PV.

articleTitle: Readiness Index for Indonesian Power Plant toward Industry 4.0
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Implementation of Industry 4.0 in Indonesia can improve product quality, leverage productivity, and increasing product efficiency. Therefore, it will increase industrial competitiveness. In order to boost the industrial transformation towards Industry 4.0, PT. PLN as the main electricity provider in Indonesia needs of an indexing tool that can be utilized to measure the readiness of power plant in Indonesia. This is the base of the formulation of the index named Indonesia Industry 4.0 Readiness Index for Power Plant or abbreviated as INDI 4.0 - Power Plant. In INDI 4.0 - Power Plant there are five pillars that need to be measured, which is: management and organization, people and culture, connectivity, digitalization, and technology. From these five pillars, it is further divided into 15 fields. From these 15 fields the readiness reference is taken to measure Indonesian power plant transformation towards Industry 4.0. From the early assessment done in the early 2019, the result obtained shows that the average index score in Indonesia is in level 2. It means the power plant readiness to transform towards Industry 4.0 is in "intermediate" stage. From the study also shows that INDI 4.0 - Power Plant can effectively use as the standard reference to measure the readiness of the power plant in Indonesia to transform towards Industry 4.0.

articleTitle: A Grid-connected Inverter with VAr Support Capability for A Small Scale Solar PV Using A Droop Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: This paper presents a grid-connected inverter with VAr support capability implemented in a small scale solar PV system. This system is used to support reactive power balance in low voltage distribution network as the imbalance reactive power between supply and demand may increase energy losses in distribution lines. The reactive power control in this method adopts a droop technique. The control method includes phase-locked loop in order to confirm the synchronism between the inverter and grid. Besides, harmonics is one of the important issues in a grid-connected inverter and hence we should accommodate this problem in the controller design. Several experiments have been carried out to test the effectiveness of the design and the results show that the proposed design can be used as an alternative method of controlling VAr.

articleTitle: Co-firing RDF in CFB Boiler Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Biomass co-firing in coal fired power plant especially in circulating fluidized bed (CFB) boiler is being tested in several power plants in the world. This report addresses operational issue for cofiring refused derived fuel (RDF) in circulating fluidized bed boiler. The main operational parameters being monitored are temperature and pressure distribution in the furnace, which are represent the fluidization condition and fuel combustion itself. Another operational parameter needed to be monitored are flue gas compositions which are represent the emission effect of the fuel type. The RDF used in this cofiring produce in Klungkung-Bali, which is produce from local municipal solid waste with bio-drying method developed by STT PLN. The RDF produced by this method can reach calorific value around 3270 kcal/kg, with more than 95% organic matters containment. During cofiring application at 5% RDF, the main parameter changes only on furnace pressure differential which is rise up the amount of excess air (O2) was indicated to be 6% higher and CO2 was 4% lower. RDF pellets also contain less sulfur when compared to coal, the lower SO2 and H2S indicates a reduction in sulfur emissions. The lower NOx shows a positive indication of a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions.

articleTitle: Determination of Overhead Conductors Curves with Quadratic Approach Based
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Transmission line conductor supported by towers will cause sag in the conductor span. Sag is an unavoidable condition related with the weight and the limited tensile strength of the high voltage overhead conductor. Sag is also influenced by elevation angle, span distance , wind speed, and temperature. The main purpose of sag determination is to obtain a safe distance (free area) of the object under the overhead conductor and to determine the conductor length and tower height. This paper proposes a calculation method with the quadratic approach that is influenced by elevation angles, distance ranges, wind speed, and temperature. The methodology is based on mathematical derivation to obtain the formulations clearly. This method has been tested by simulation to understand the effect of elevation angle, wind speed, and temperature on the sag. The simulation results show that the proposed method has been able to determine the conductor curve along the span distance for various angles of height. From this conductor curve, the clearance area under the conductor can be determined precisely. A small increase in the conductor due to the temperature rise leads to a significant increase in sag (2.80m) compared to the influence of the wind with a pressure of 40kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (sag increases 1.18m). Increased elevation angle will reduce the sag to the lowest tower and will increase the sag to the highest tower. When the angle is 1.374° and span distance 350m, the obtained sag for the lowest tower is zero and for the highest tower obtained the same height difference between the two towers (tower 1 and tower 2). This elevation angle also affects the length of the conductor, for the elevation angle changes from 1° to 5° and the lenght of the conductor rises linearly.

articleTitle: Comparison of Static Var Compensator (SVC) and Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) for Static Voltage Stability Based on Sensitivity Analysis : A Case Study of 500 KV Java-Bali Electrical Power System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Demand for electricity is increasing rapidly, the consequence of this is a threat to the stability of the electrical system, one of which is the voltage stability. FACTS or flexible alternating current transmission system is electronic equipment capable of regulating electrical power transmission that can be used to overcome stability problems. This study will analyze the comparison of SVC use with UPFC as an equipment model from FACTS to overcome the stability of the electric power system on the most critical buses. Simulations are carried out using PSAT using a case study: a 500 kV JavaBali network. Then the stability of the voltage is observed using the help of the PV curve which can show the value of the voltage conditions in each operating condition. SVC installation in the Java-Bali 500 kV case does not reduce the active power losses or reactive power, but also the addition of length λ is 0.233 p.u. (6.01%) and compared to the addition of length λ in the UPFC of 0.38 p.u. (9.82%) and there is a reduction in active power losses of 0.002 p.u. or 0.203% but there is an increase in reactive power losses of 0.007 p.u. or equal to 0.676%.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging Load Forecasting Model Considering Road Network-Power Grid Information
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: With the rapid development of electric vehicles, it is important to predict the charging load of electric vehicles for the power grid. Considering that both the road network and the power grid have an impact on the charging load of electric vehicles, this paper proposes a charging load forecasting model based on the interactive architecture of the road network and the power grid. Firstly, the travel destination is obtained from the vehicle travel characteristics, and the specific driving process of the vehicle is simulated by microscopic traffic simulation. Then, the power flow is calculated in real time according to the current load, and the charging price is changed synchronously by the node voltage. Finally, predict the space-time distribution of electric vehicle charging load and study the impact of charging load on the power grid. Taking Beijing Third Ring Road Network model and IEEE30 node grid as an example, the charging load of EV is predicted, and the validity of the model is verified. The simulation results show that the distribution of charging load of taxi and private car is quite different in time and space, the charging load makes the grid voltage drop seriously.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Cogging Torque Reduction of Integral Slot Number in Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Optimize the cogging torque reduction in permanent magnet machine was investigated in this paper, with the proposed machine of 48 stator slots and 6 poles. The slot opening proposed model width has been fixed to 2 mm. The two steps of slotting have been employed and assessed to reduce the cogging torque of the proposed model. In this study, the finite element method tool was implemented to investigate the magnetic flux distribution and the cogging torque reduction of the proposed model. The Response Surface Method (RSM) as one optimization technique has been implemented. By applying the finite element method, simulation results showed that the cogging torque of the PMMs proposed model could decrease effectively. In this study, the cogging torque reduction for the proposed model as much as 98.8 % compared with the initial model.

articleTitle: Modelling Hybrid PV-Generator System Using MATLAB/Simulink at Jifak Village, Papua
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Solar irradiation is clean, readily available, abundant and is famous as a renewable energy source. Solar Photovoltaic (PV) system power plant with the hybrid system is introduced as a potential solution to fulfil electricity demand for off-grid areas, such as Jifak Village, Asmat Regency, Papua. In 2018, the electricity network coverage area was only 57.03% in Papua Province, Indonesia. On the other side, this region consistently receives high solar radiation intensity for an average 4.68 kWh/m2 per year. The research objective was designing suitable hybrid Photovoltaic (PV) system module, which will be utilized further in Jifak Village, Asmat Regency. This developed hybrid PV System model was featuring PV module, a boost converter, Maximum Power Point Tracker (MPPT) method with applied Incremental Conductance Algorithm for tracking maximum power point, storage battery model, a single-phase inverter model, generator set (Genset) and communal load model. Hybrid PV system model was developed using MATLAB/SIMULINK program, and HOMER Pro program was used for a feasibility study on the economic value of this system. MATLAB/SIMULINK program chosen due to its customization capability for hourly data input. Meanwhile, HOMER Pro program was only accommodating average monthly data input. MATLAB/SIMULINK customization ability was the driving system for incorporating more comprehensive PV performance. In this research, the proposed model showed that maximum power point was always located at the expected position, readily tracked, and maintained by increasing and decreasing irradiation profile variable. The research also showed that energy output, equal to at least 40 kWh was able to supply electricity as the communal load for 100 households in Jifak Village, Asmat Regency, Papua province.

articleTitle: NaCl Doped LiNi0.8Co0.15Al0.05O2 via Solid-State Reaction for Li-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: NCA (LiNi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</sub>Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) cathode material is a promising cathode material for Lithium-Ion (Li-ion) Battery due to its low toxicity, low production cost, long cycle life, and high specific capacity compare to LiCoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (LCO) cathode. Therefore, extensive research has been reported in order to obtain high-quality NCA powder. Modification to enhance the characteristics and performance of NCA using cheap material is an interesting topic to be discussed. Therefore the purpose of this research is to investigate material processing, sintering temperature, and the effect of adding NaCl toward NCA characteristic and performance via simple solid-state reaction at high temperature. NaCl concentration of 1%, 3%, 5%, 7%, and 20% were added to the precursor. The crystal structure was tested using XRD (X-Ray Diffraction). Electrochemical performance of NCA was tested in an NCA/graphite system at 2.7 - 4.2 volt and 1/10 C rate. Based on the result, the addition of NaCl results in increasing crystallite size. However, at higher NaCl content, impurities are observed in the XRD pattern. In conclusion, the optimum NaCl concentration is established at 3% with the initial specific capacity of 71.27 mAh/g discharge.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of PV Module and the Effect on its Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The performance of a photovoltaic (PV) module depends on some factors, such as the variation of solar radiation, convection heat transfer coefficient and temperature. The aim of this work is to consider the performance of the silicon-based PV module through the thermal analysis by using ANSYS software. The PV module consists of glass, ethyl vinyl acetate (EVA), solar cell, EVA, and polyvinyl fluoride (PVF) from top to bottom. The simulation of the heat loss using ANSYS is obtained by the thermal conductivity of the materials, the different convection, and different solar irradiation. The environmental condition of PV module, with solar radiation 1000 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, convective heat coefficient 8 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and ambient temperature 25°C, makes the module temperature to 47.15°C and the estimated efficiency to 13.50%. As the increase of the ambient temperature to 50°C, the estimated efficiency goes down to 11.82%. Since the temperature increases, the efficiency of the PV module will decrease. Meanwhile, the decrease of solar irradiation at 500 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> makes the improvement of estimated PV efficiency at 14.25%, which means the thermal management of the PV module is very important for the PV applications.

articleTitle: Financial Risk Assessment For Power Plant Investment Under Uncertainty Using Monte Carlo Simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Financial analysis is an important part of a feasibility study for an investment. In order to show that an investment is profitable or not, normally people use some methods such as Net Present Value (NPV), Payback Period, Benefit/Cost Ratio (B/C Ratio), Internal Rate of Return (IRR) and Modified Internal Rate of Return (MIRR). However, many people who work as a financial analysis normally only use a deterministic approach when they did a feasibility study for investment. In fact there are many uncertainty factors, i.e. exchange rate, in financial analysis of feasibility study. This uncertainty factors can be considered as risks. Many previous researches have been trying to capture this phenomenon. They use the Monte Carlo Simulation called NPV@risk. Unfortunately, the NPV@Risk uses paid license software called @Risk. And for some people or institution who cannot afford it, it could be a problem. Furthermore, in 2018, the ISO replace ISO 31000:2009 with the ISO 31000:2018. Thus, this research is an update of the previous research who work on integration of Risk Management framework and NPV@risk (Monte Carlo Simulation) using a free license software for Monte Carlo. To test the method, the case of power plant investment in 2007 is used. We use some variable, identified as risk, such as coal price, exchange rate, fuel price, etc. Using our proposed framework, one can capture that the impact on an increase of coal price leads to a catastrophic consequence. Furthermore, based on our risk map, the increase of coal price can be identified as a catastrophic risk. Thus, one could propose a long term contract of coal price in order to mitigate this type of risk and increase the success rate of the project.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study on Installation of Solar Cell Renewable Energy Generators
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The need of electrical energy is currently increasing, both in the community and in the industrial environment. Conventional power plants owned by the government today, are unable to meet the national energy demand which continue to increase each year. The purpose of this research is to provide information about the construction of plants in an area which be used as a provider of electricity for the community. In this research, HOMER software was used to design a renewable energy generating system that originated from the sun. HOMER software's function is to optimize the size of the generator, especially the constituent components of solar power plants, so that the generation of electrical energy is more economical as a provider of electricity reserves. The results of electrical energy generated from the design of solar power generation systems (Photo Voltaic) amounted to 235,322 kWh. Renewable penetration of components in generating electrical energy is 61% of the total electrical energy produced. The Cost of Energy (COE) issued per 1 kWh is Rp. 990 / kWh and the Net Present Cost (NPC) in the construction of a solar power plant is Rp. 3,014,315,178. Whereas the annualized cost of maintenance of components of solar power plants in a year is Rp. 233,170,475. And the payback period is 14 years and 1 month..

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis Between Fixed Tilt And Tracked PV System In Tropical Climate
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Climate change, rising fuel cost and cost reduction of renewable energy power generation have pushed the development of this technology to develop expeditiously. The condition in Indonesia, especially the eastern part of Indonesia which consists of islands make the electrical system distributed. Conventional power plants that might be used to power electricity to this island is only a diesel generator system (DG). The impact is PLN suffered heavy losses because the tariffs of diesel generator were far higher than the electricity tariffs in general. Photovoltaic power generation (PV) can compete with the diesel generator tariff. Regrettably, this competition is also influenced by fluctuations in fuel prices and political economic conditions that can change the DG tariff any time. PT PJB conducts research to make PV system tariff more competitive than DG to optimize the production of PV based on the types of PV mounting systems including fixed tilt, single and dual axis tracker installed on grid system with the aim of proving the type of mounting system that is suitable for tropical regions, especially in Indonesia. The results of PT PJB's research prove that solar PV with tracking system is very suitable to be installed in tropical climate areas. It is proven by the percentage of output energy and specific yield tracking greater than the fix tilt system is equal to 13,17% (single axis and 23,56% (dual axis).

articleTitle: Controlling Energy Consumption of Building under Intelligent Control System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The aim of this research is to evaluate the energy consumption of buildings under intelligent control system. There are two kinds of building was investigated, such us: building-1 with using an innovative Cellular Lightweight Concrete (CLC) brick and building-2 with using traditional CLC brick. Under the Intelligent control system, the energy consumption of buildings was controlled based on the outside temperature. To achieve this goal, a simulation model under intelligent control system was developed to evaluate the minimum cost of air conditioning (AC) for both of buildings. Based on result of research indicated the energy consumption of building-1 and building-2 were IDR 24784 and IDR 29600, respectively. Consequently, the energy saving was IDR 4816 (16.27%).

articleTitle: Characteristics of Temperature Changes Measurement on Photovoltaic Surfaces Against Quality of Output Current on Solar Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Renewable energy sources have a renewable and sustainable nature and the utilization of renewable energy sources is an alternative energy that needs to be developed further. In this research, a Characteristics Study of Temperature Changes on Photovoltaic Surfaces against the Quality of Output Current in Solar Power Plants are measured, and it is known that the optimum current value is at 1.92 Ampere, the optimum temperature is at 37.4 °C, and the highest exchange rate is at 2.08 Ampere while the temperature on the surface of the solar cell is at 37.4 °C. In accordance with the results, which have been done by using a mathematical regression equation that is the statistical equation quadratic regression, it can be known that the characteristics of solar cells have an efficient workforce is around 37.4 °C.

articleTitle: Impact of Plug In Electric Vehicle on Uniformly Distributed System Model
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Rising price and decreasing reserves of fossil fuels make electric vehicles a future transportation choice. In addition, awareness to reduce CO2 emissions also encourages the use of public and private electric cars. The increasing need for private electric vehicles will definitely be followed by the addition of plug-in electric vehicles (PEV), especially in residential areas. The PEV penetration in the residential area will directly impact power quality of the secondary distribution networks. Uniformly distributed distribution model using real recorded daily load profile and EV charging model are conducted and designed in power system analysis software to understand the impact of PEV penetration in residential areas. The simulation result shows that voltage drop and line loading increase significantly due to PEV overnight charging and relative to the percentage of penetration and location of PEV installation. Peak shifting is possibly happening during the PEV charging process. The line loading could reach more than 100% loading as the impact of increasing PEV penetration. The overloading condition will overheat the conductor and possibly impact the distribution equipment lifetime.

articleTitle: Environmentally Friendly Synthesis of LiNi0.80Co0.15Al0.05O2 Cathode Material for Li-ion Batteries and Its Galvanostic Test Using Artificial Graphite Anode
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Homogenous LiNi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,15</sub>Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (NCA) cathode material can be obtained via co-precipitation of salt solution. In the co-precipitation method, ammonia is commonly used as chelating agent to control the crystal growth and reaction kinetics. However, continuous use of ammonia as chelating agent during NCA synthesis rises health and environmental issue due to toxic properties of such chemical. Hence, a suitable and green chelating agent in preparing NCA cathode material is needed. EDTA-2Na (di-sodium Ethylene Diamine Tetra-acetic Acid) is an alternative environmental friendly chelating agent. The use of inexpensive carbonate salt as precipitant is also promising to be adapted in such process. Therefore this study aims to produce NCA using batch carbonate co-precipitation with EDTA-2Na as its sole chelating agent. Structural analysis was deeply investigated. The morphology and surface chemistry of as prepared NCA is characterized using SEM, FTIR, and XRF. The electrochemical test is carried out in an 18650 cylindrical battery. Meso Carbon Micro Beads (MCMB) was used as the counter anode. The specific capacity of its sample was tested at a voltage of 2.7 to 4.25 V and the current of 1/10 C. The results show the as prepared NCA has a specific initial discharge capacity of 63.2 mAh/gram.

articleTitle: The Overview of Turbine’s Rotor Repair Methodology in 55 MW Geothermal Powerplant
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The 55 MW Geothermal power plant located in West Java, suffered a Turbine's broken into 2 parts in the workshop during processing of crack relieved from the turbine rotor. The root cause assessment indicates that the severely damage on turbine crack is due to harsh operational environment, highly acid geo-fluid from the reservoir.The standard procedure to relieve the crack is by machining deep in to the crack and re-welding to the original size, and further machining to meet the original size of the rotor. Therefore, since the crack was depth enough close to the center of the rotor, during machining the rotor was broken, there is no standard procedure available for rotor turbin's repairement. Considering take or pay of supplying steam the immediate and prudent action shall be taken to reduce a high operation loss, while to avoiding sluggish purchasing of the new rotor option.Development of new methodology for the broken rotor repairing procedure is highly concern on technical aspect that qualify to pass an approved quality assurance based on international standard available. The proposed repairing methodology is by using a procedure of stub-weld method with a comprehensive quality check to assure quality process in each repair stage. Finally, the success rotor stub-weld method within 8 months, has return the powerplant's performance, and much faster recovery duration compared with procure a new purchasing turbine's rotor option.

articleTitle: Optimal Tuning of PID Control on Single Machine Infinite Bus Using Ant Colony Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Sudden changes in the load on the electric power system will cause a dynamic disturbance. This interference causes the generator stability to be disrupted because the generator does not respond to the interference quickly. This causes oscillations in the generator in the form of frequency oscillations and rotor angles. One additional control equipment that can improve the stability of a generator is the Power System Stabilizer (PID). When there is a disturbance oscillation on the generator, the PID provides an additional signal to the excitation equipment to provide additional attenuation to the generator. The use of PID is needed to coordinate the determination of the right parameters to achieve good performance control for the system. In the application, the determination of PID parameters still uses the trial & error method, this method is very difficult to get the right parameters. To solve this problem, here the author uses one of the computational techniques (soft computing) artificial intelligence, namely the Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm to optimize the tuning of the PID parameters. From the simulation results, the optimal PID parameters obtained are P (Proportional) of 53.4899, I (Integral) of 14.6551, and D (Derivative) of 10.5383. With optimal tuning, the SMIB frequency response is perfect compared to the system without PID trial error control and control, this is indicated by the system response that has improved, where the controller is able to provide stability so that the overshoot oscillation can be muted, and the settling time performance is faster for the system goes to steady-state condition. By tuning the right PID parameters, Overshoot that occurs in this system can be muted that is equal to -0.0002609 up to 0.0001954.

articleTitle: Study of AGC in The Sarawak - West Kalimantan Interconnected Power System under Deregulated Scenario
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: In the SEB interconnection and renewable energy sources, the West Kalimantan power system should prepare large reserve capacities for unexpected transmission line disconnection or connection. We suggest how to design supply- demand balance strategies for stable operations under unexpected situations for the SESCO-West Kalimantan power system interconnection and large-scale PLTU insertion in the West Kalimantan power system. They are connected in parallel for the power generation system. In Transmission Control Center, these ESSs are installed on idle capital of a substation to regulate the frequency. In Sektor Kapuas (Generation Coordinator), they are installed on a generation plant. At least four biomass power generation (PLTBm) are scheduled to be completed in West Kalimantan by 2019 as part of a high biomass-potential resources such as wood, palm oil, and agricultural residues, production utilized by developers of power plants/independent power producer (IPP). Because of these energy exchanges, both environmental problems and the supply/demand unbalance of energy may increase in SEA countries. In addition, the control mechanism of interconnection system responsible for maintaining the system frequency to the nominal value and the real power interchange between balancing authority areas to the scheduled values is referred to as Automatic Generation Control (AGC). AGC is a system for adjusting the power output of multiple generators at different power plants, in response to changes in the load. This paper presents the SESCO-West Kalimantan power system interconnection (SEB-PSI), distributed energy resources-based operation strategies targeting supply-demand balance and performance of the AGC system in Indonesia and Malaysia.

articleTitle: Development of Coal Fired Power Plant Aging Fly Ash and Bottom Ash Utilization
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Suralaya Coal Fired Power Plant (CFPP), with 3400 MW total capacity, contribute for 7.8% of the Java Bali transmission system load. Hazardous waste in form of fly ash bottom ash from Suralaya CFPP around 486,000 tons/year, consisting of fly ash 375,000 tons and bottom ash 111,000 tons. This research aims to maximize the composition of aging fly ash bottom ash (FABA) as raw material in lightweight aggregate (LWA) and nonstructural concrete products i.e. paving blocks, coarse aggregates and concrete panel fence. Testing was carried out until 90% mass composition of aging fly ash bottom ash per product. To ensure the product quality as result of FABA utilization, several tests were carried out such as compressive strength, material abrasion, material gradation, specific gravity and material absorption, and splitting tensile strength. From the abrasion test results, the lightweight aggregate has value 72.86% (the average natural aggregate has value <; 50%), fineness modulus 6.38 (average 6.3-6.9), and compressive strength 37.8-39.8 MPa at curing age of 28 days. The product meets the criteria of products standard of lightweight aggregate and concrete. By assuming the price of product 80% lower from market price, the economic value obtained can cover the investment costs and annual operational costs.

articleTitle: HEPAF and IGVM Combination Technology to Control the Industrial Gas Turbine Performance, Excess Air and CO2 Production
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Technology variant application in the power plant have a significant impact on the performance, the main targeted area in the latest technology application are increase the power plant efficiency, decrease CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> production and reliability of power plant engine, this area can be applied for F series of gas turbine at muara karang power plant. In F series gas turbine, inlet guide vane modulation application (IGVM) has an effect on power plant efficiency, the mechanism of IGVM works by setting the IGV opening at partial load. This mechanism will cost 150 million rupiahs for minor modifications and spare parts on IGV, however the investment cost will return only in two weeks operating time because of the combined cycle efficiency increase 0.7% (8 kCal/kWh) and also decrease 0,5 % the CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> production. High efficiency particulate air Filter (HEPAF) used to maintain the air quality enter the gas turbine compressor. If the air entering the compressor without impurity particles, the compressor efficiency will keep in high. With HEPAF the power plant efficiency can be maintained and the efficiency reduction value that can be avoided reaches 1.2% (14 kCal/kWh). HEPAF will need four billion rupiahs investment for new filters and medium modification at intake air duct, but this investment will return in 8 months operating time compared with not using HEPAF unit. As a summary, the result shows after the application use for F series gas turbine, the program that will affect efficiency and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> production is IGVM, and the application that maintains efficiency is HEPAF, and this combination (IGVM and HEPAF) already proven in muara karang power plant.

articleTitle: Implementation of Risk Analysis using Monte Carlo Simulation on Electricity Investment Decision Making : Case Study: Steam and Combined Cycle Power Plant Development in Indonesia by PT Pembangkitan Jawa-Bali
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: In order to support the development of national economic, the government of Indonesia has issued a breakthrough program called development of 35GW to provide electricity accross nation. The composition of the power plant in this program is still dominated by conventional power plants, namely steam and combined cycle power plant with composition 60% and 21% respectively. A huge capital of Rp 1,200 trillion is required to support the 35GW program. With these huge capital requirements, the risk of developing this project will also increase. For this reason, investors like PT Pembangkitan Jawa-Bali (PJB) need to make investment decisions that consider comprehensive risk analysis. In the initial stage, identification of risk factors is required to create the mapping of the risk factors that affect the cash flow through investment activities in power plant development. The next step is conducting the risk factor evaluation to determine the critical risk factor. Furthermore, risk analysis is carried out using simulation methods, one of which is Monte Carlo simulation. The aim of Monte Carlo simulation is to produce large number of outputs of varying financial parameters based on changes in the value of critical risk factors. Based on the results of risk factor evaluation, the risk factors that significantly influence the development of steam and combined cycle power plant in Indonesia are EPC Cost, Net Plant Heat Rate and Debt to Equity Ratio. By conducting risk analysis using Monte Carlo simulation, a range of Internal Rate of Return value is obtained and can be used as a guide in making investment decisions. Electricity investment decision making that considers comprehensive risk analysis will produce optimal rate of return that will lead to a decrease in Basic Cost of Supply (BPP) of PT PLN (Persero).

articleTitle: Learning Vector Quantization Based Vibration Analysis for Steam Power Plant Rotating Equipment Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Sudden failure of rotating equipment in a steam power plant can cause a sudden electrical power outage and economical losses. Rotating equipment in a base load steam power plant operated in a non stop loading. Vibration data is able to be extracted from rotating equipment, which is used in vibration analysis to predict early symptom of rotating equipment fault. A Learning Vector Quantization (LVQ) based vibration analysis is able to give a quick and objective analysis based on its learning data. A normalized spectral data of rotating equipment vibration is used as input variables for the LVQ algorithm to perform vibration analysis. The normalized spectral data which is used as training and analysis data is based on literature and empirical data. In this study the LVQ model is used to learn and classify five failure symptoms in power plant rotating equipment. The proposed method can achieve 100% accuracy in three cases, unbalance, parallel misalignment, and cocked bearing. Angular misalignment and bent shaft have not been tested because no actual case happened. Additional training of LVQ algorithm will upgrade the knowledge base.

articleTitle: Study of Determining Cost Compensation of Power Wheeling Transaction on Composite System Reliability by Optimal Power Flow
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Transmission lines access will widely open to encourage industry to produce its power through power wheeling mechanism. Power wheeling can optimize the use of the transmission network. However, power wheeling will affect power system reliability. This study calculates EENS that describes the energy did not serve for one year (MWh/year). The cost resulting from the change of EENS is then calculated using a multiplier factor of VoLL (Value of Lost Load). The cost resulted due to changes in EENS will be compared with the cost of power wheeling calculated with absolute MVA-km method. The proposed method was tested on the IEEE Reliability Test System (IEEE RTS). The aim is to find a cost compensation of power wheeling transaction. The results show that power wheeling can change power system reliability and it is influenced by the amount of power transmitted, power flow, and bus location. If power wheeling transaction decreases the reliability thus it increased EENS value, additional fees will be charged to the user of power wheeling. Conversely, a discount will be given when power wheeling transactions decrease EENS value so that it increased the system reliability.

articleTitle: On Digital Power Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: In this paper, the integration of digital transmission system and power transmission system using switching power converter is presented. The proposed concept can be referred as a Digital Power Transmission system. The aim is to provide electric power for residential, commercial and industrial loads as well as to deliver data, audio or video information to customers. This paper focused on Digital DC Power Transmission system based on buck converter topology. The proposed digital power transmission system has specification of 400 V dc input voltage, 2 Mbps data rate with unipolar NRZ (Non-Return to Zero) line coding and three point of loads in the range of 1.1 - 1.9 kW. The voltage and current stresses of semiconductor devices will be analyzed in this paper. In addition, the behavior of current and voltage waveforms will be simulated and discussed. The analysis of the converter in CCM (Continuous Conduction Mode) operation based on digital input signal is also provided. The method to extract and separate DC output power from digital output signal is also discussed. Simulation results confirm that the digital output signal with data rate of 2 Mbps is the same as the digital input signal, and the output power can be extracted to the loads without introducing harmful functions.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Lubricated Journal Bearing Under Surface Roughness Arrangement
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Journal bearings as machine elements have always been of particular interest due to widespread applications. However, high level of power loss limits the reliability of lubricated journal bearing. The current paper explores the possibility of employing the artificial roughness in bearing in order to enhance performance behavior based on computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis. The hydrodynamic performance is calculated by Navier-Stokes equation coupled with continuity equation with finite volume method. In order to obtain more accurate results, the multiphase cavitation model is also considered in the computation. The hydrodynamic pressure as well as the load support is presented for two kinds of loading (low vs high) varying the surface roughness levels. The results show that for heavy loaded bearing, the surface roughness has an important influence on the lubrication characteristics of the bearing, while for light loaded one, the surface roughness effect is not so significant. This study contributes to the improvement of the journal bearing performance.

articleTitle: Double Air Terminal in Lightning Protection System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Air terminal system prevents lightning from directly strike critical buildings and equipments. This is a well-known protection system in oil and gas industry. Double air terminal works by reducing the ignition in cold vent stack. In this study, double air terminal with height variations is simulated using COMSOL Multiphysics® software. The variation of double air terminal position have been simulated resulting electric field distribution near vent stack. The result shows that double air terminal reduced electrical field near cold vent stack, which indirectly reduced the probability of ignition.

articleTitle: Smart Grid Initiatives in South East Asian Countries : What Are Being Done in The Early Stage
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Factors such as the increasing complexity of power grid; state-of-the-art operation and information technology; more complex behavior and characteristics of customers' loads; the unstoppable demands of better quality, reliability, and efficiency of electricity; and the growing development of renewable energy sources have become challenges for power utilities to build and implement smarter grids. Several countries in Europe and United States answered these challenges by deploying projects towards Smart Grid, in which various different key initiatives were introduced in the initial phase in different countries with different power grid structures and problems. In the same sense, South East Asian countries have also carried out key initiatives to tackle challenges mentioned above. This paper is intended to give insights on the smart grid key initiatives taken by each utility under HAPUA, especially in the distribution system. All data presented here were gathered first hand from all utilities under Head of ASEAN Power Utilities/Authorities (HAPUA). Subsequently, a table of commonness of key initiatives was created to find out which initiatives became the most selected ones. Based on the table of commonness, it appears that AMI, AMR, and SCADA were the most common key initiatives taken by the majority.

articleTitle: Lightning Detection Monitoring System For Identification Transmission Line Fault in PLN Trans JBT
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Transmission line fault case in PLN Trans-JBT from year 2015 till 2017 are dominated by tower accessories damage (42%) and then by lightning strike (27%) from total 557 case, this is due to high density of lightning strike in tropical area such as in Java Island (Indonesia). Previously, fault analysis data is only obtained from Disturbance Fault Recorder (DFR) and Fault Locator (FL) in the Substation. PLN Trans JBT did not have lightning detector. Evaluation of the performance lightning detection monitoring system in PLN Trans JBT has been carried out by regional analysis, exposure analysis and reliability analysis. The purpose of this paper present evaluation of the performance lightning strike detection network on power transmission line systems. The mean, median and standard deviation of the Substation (SS) to CG vs. Fault locator distance were 2.95 km, 2.63 km and 2.70 km respectively. Since LDMS implemented in April 2017, PLN Trans JBT have optimized the use of LDMS for further inspection and maintenance improvement such as additional ground rod tower, insulator string replacement and earth wire replacement so that lightning fault trending can decrease significantly from 2016 till March 2018 (60%).

articleTitle: Opportunity Cost Allocation for Wheeling Using Power Flow Tracing
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Wheeling can change production cost on utility whose network that used for wheeling operation. This change comes from forced dispatch because of the addition generator and wheeling load. The value that appears from forced dispatch is called opportunity cost. Opportunity cost must be distributed among wheeling subjects fairly. This cost is counted based on marginal cost differences between before and after wheeling implemented. This research aims to allocate opportunity cost caused by wheeling. Opportunity cost allocation among wheeling subjects is calculated using Kirschen tracing method. The result shows that opportunity cost allocated more fairly to wheeling subjects using this method. The result shows that the opportunity cost because two-wheeling operations are allocated to the wheeling subject A and B according to their contribution. The wheeling A gets an opportunity cost allocation of 504.17 $/hr and wheeling B receives an allocation of 777.86 $/hr.

articleTitle: Energy Loss Analysis using Value Stream Mapping (VSM): a Power Plant Case Study
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Value stream mapping (VSM) is powerful and effective to map out processes and to eliminate critical issues. This paper describes the application of VSM to reduce energy loss in a power plant. In doing so, three stages of the proposed VSM were used, namely (1) mapping the big picture and the process flow, (2) identifying the potential energy loss, and (3) analyzing and determining the future state. At the first stage, using observations and interviews, the big picture and the process flow was mapped out to understand the main suppliers and customers, as well as the main process in the power plant. At the second stage, energy loss equations and heat energy rate analysis were used to identify and analyze the potential energy losses. At the final stage, the analysis identified the top three energy loss stages in the unloading process, the top two energy loss stages in the loading process, and the top five energy loss stages in the electricity generation process. The implication of this study is outlined in the conclusion to improve VSM in the future.

articleTitle: Digitalization Solution on Customer Services to Leverage the Ease of Getting Electricity
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: As one the public industries, one of the challenges in the electricity business is to have an excellent customer services. One of those services may support and lever the company's index of the Ease of Getting Electricity which Indonesia now has scored 87,06 (on a scale of 100). With the power of digitalization, cognitive technologies, and tools, human resources operation will empower employees and the organization to serve the business and the customers. This paper will show information and communication technology (ICT) that is used as tools by the state-owned electricity company to face the disruption of the electricity business and operational improvement nationwide by implementing a workflow automation on several customer service functions as well as an automatic performance indicator. The tools comprise web-based and mobile applications that will automate distribution of work order and manage tasks performed by employees so that stakeholders can transparently track, monitor, and control the result. At the end of the service delivery, it will allow customers to give ratings or suggestions to improve the services. By the end of the performance period, management can give rewards to the employees that have the best performances in delivering the services. Briefly, by implementing workflow automation and performance indicators, the employee engagement increases up to 26.1%, affecting the reduction of the disruption impact in the electricity business to the organization by 35.4%, and the improvement of the operational excellence service level by 65.7%, as well as customer satisfaction in a period of 2 (two) years.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-PID Controller On MPPT PV To Stabilize DC Bus Voltage
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The energy generated by solar cells varies greatly depending on weather conditions and because the solar energy is changing at any time, the power generated is also changed and not maximum. To achieve high efficiency Maximum Power Point Tracker is used. In this paper we will use fuzzy PID method as MPPT controller on PV. Fuzzy logic is used to optimize the PID in the tracking of the maximum power point, so that the voltage or output power of the boost converter will always be stable. Fuzzy input is power and irradiation, while the output is the change of PID parameters to be used to set the boost converter. In this fuzzy design the intensity of solar energy from 1w / m2 to 1000 w / m2, while the solar cell power capacity from 1watt to 1000 watts and temperature temperature at 25 ° C. From the simulation results on the picture shows that the PID controller produces a larger overshoot when compared to the fuzzy PID controller, the overshoot generated by the PID controller is 15.14 percent with the rise time of 0.043 seconds. While the fuzzy PID controller produces 2.1 percent overshoot with 0.036 second rise time.

articleTitle: Implementation of Fault Current Limiter in West Java 150 KV Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Fault current limiter (FCL) is a novel approach in protecting equipment from excessive fault current. In this paper, the whole implementation process of FCL devices is presented. There are two families of modern FCL technology, namely superconducting FCL (SFCL) and pre-saturated core FCL (PCFCL), each with its own techno-economic characteristics. The advantages and disadvantages of each technology will be explored and be compared with the conventional current limiting device, i.e. series reactor. Sizing and calculation processes, as well as design criteria of each equipment, will be presented. We hypothesized that series reactor as the cheapest current-limiter device would be able to mitigate the fault current problem while maintaining the system's reliability and efficiency. This hypothesis is based on our observation that in West Java 150 kV system, large fault current flows through bus-tie. On the other hand, no significant current flow through bus-tie was observed in normal condition. Lastly, we present the challenges and lessons learned in implementing FCL from a design project executed together by PLN Enjiniring and PLN TJBB in West Java 150 kV transmission network.

articleTitle: Losses Management of PT. PLN (Persero) ULP Siak by Using Jogja Losses Formula Calculation Method
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: As solely company to manages electricity in Indonesia PT. PLN (Persero) often suffer from business loss due to the following reason, i.g. vulnerability power, unsecure risk, improper finance cost, unknown billing target for street's lighting. To anticipate those problem PLN has conducted best practice in term of losses management which known by Jogja Losses Formula. This paper proposed this method for PT. PLN (Persero) ULP Siak to overcome above mentioned problems. Jogja Losses Formula method has several mechanisms to perform analysis. Firstly, collect the data assets, production's data, and selling's data according to the unit's condition. Then, the process continue by Jogja Losses Formula to get each losses value. The result was presented in Chart Dupont which divide losses into two part, i.e. technical losses and non-technical losses, so we can evaluate and analyst the losses. Based on the data calculation, PLN Siak on February 2016 shows the high range losses still remain with 11,59% total losses. Overalls, Jogja Losses Formula has proven for PLN Siak able to obtained the exact value of total losses line distribution and successfully to achieve the target into 7,35% by December 2016.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis on Wireless Power Transfer for Continuous Charging of a Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) is not a new finding in Electrical Engineering technology; however, currently, it is back to fame due to the increment of device mobility, avoiding the hazardous wiring application, cleaner connection, and improves vehicle mobility. The WPT can be an alternative to power an automatic transport system that results in an aesthetic and safe system. The continuous charging ensures system reliability. The main problem with WPT is that it is still limited by the distance, which can be overcome by setting the transmitter and receiver in a sufficient distance. This paper discussed the prototype of automated transport and simulated using a line follower mobile robot, which is charged continuously by a WPT system. The proposed method is tested by two experimental test-bed settings; the under the track and overhead transmitter setting. The produced voltage and currents move the robot at a different speed that is achieved by varying the distance between transmitter and receiver. The ideal distance between transmitter and receiver attached to the line follower robot is 2 cm indicated by DC motor speed. For under the track transmitter setting, at the distance of 2 cm, the robot's DC motor moves in 104.5 RPM, and for the overhead transmitter setting, DC motor speed is 93.4 RPM. This difference is not very significant; therefore, both applications are applicable. However, for the application in a real automated transport system, the under the track transmitter setting is aesthetically more pleasant for city planning.

articleTitle: Case Study of Straightening Methods for Bent Shaft 1.25 mm on Hip Turbine Rotor Pacitan Steam Power Plant#1
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Synchronous Failure of Pacitan#1 Steam Power Plant on December 26, 2017 to June 2018 was caused by the high vibration on the bearing so that the turbine does not reach nominal rotation (3000 rpm). This was because of the bent rotor with the highest value run out which is 1.25 mm. To overcome this problem, PJB performs several rotor straightening methods by considering three aspects, which are business, regulations and institutions. From several rotor straightening methods, an effective method for reducing rotor bending from a value of 1.25 mm to <; 0.5 mm is the thermo mechanical straightening method. The results of the thermo mechanical straightening method can reduce the maximum bending value from 1.25 mm to 0.35 mm.

articleTitle: Application of Demand Response Scheme for Generation Scheduling and Dispatch for Reducing Generation Cost
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Demand response (DR), a program motivates consumers to change their load in a period. The response load demand is being a problem in unit commitment (UC). However, UC is related to fulfilling load demand and minimizing the total operation cost of the generating unit without violation of the system and unit constraints. The UC and DR problems are solved using Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming (MIQP). Load shifting affected by the application of DR is going to affect the percentage of load factor. The higher percentage of load factor has a potential benefit for the utility. The performance of the proposed method is tested using the standard IEEE 10-unit test system. The simulation result shows that the proposed method is capable of increasing 5% load factor with DR. The simulation result also show that the proposed method is capable of reducing at 0.59% of the total generation cost.

articleTitle: Installation Of Lithium-Bromide (Li-Br) Absorption Chiller System In Cilegon Power Plant Utilizing Waste Heat From HRSG For Gas Turbine Compressor Air Intake Cooling
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Waste heat energy produced by Cilegon Combined Cycle Power Plant (Cilegon Power Plant) released to the environment through each HRSG (Heat Recovery Steam Generator) still containing large amounts of heat energy (44,759.8 kJ/s) due to massive volumetric flow (649.83 kg/s) and relatively high temperature (110 C) compared to the ambient environment temperature (28.82 C). There is potentially available technology to be used to extract this waste heat energy, namely, Lithium Bromide (Li-Br) Absorption Chiller System which can be used to converting the waste heat into chilled water and then be utilized for any cooling purpose. This research proposal mainly proposes to investigate the feasibility of implementing the Li-Br Absorption Chiller System to produce chilled water for cooling the ambient air before entering the gas turbine compressor utilizing chiller/precooler. The expected result was developed from field data during the commissioning stage in 2007, the basic steady-state energy equation which can be used to calculate the amount of energy needed to decrease the gas turbine inlet air temperature also been developed. For a decrement of 3.44 C and 28% relative humidity, it was calculated that the net power output gained and net heat rate improvement is 3.04 megawatts and -68.05 kJ/kWh respectively. Further analysis also revealed the possibility of maximizing the power output and heat rate improvement gain.

articleTitle: Boiler Reliability of 100 MW Power Plant using Reliability Block Diagram (RBD)
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The Fast Track Project Phase 1 (FTP-1) Power Plant always been an interesting issue in the field of plant reliability. Most of them had relatively lower reliability compared to non FTP-1. Based on Pareto data, the dominant and vital systems are the reliability of the Boiler system. In this research, the method to calculate reliability was approached using Reliability Block Diagram (RBD), thus the failure distribution of each equipment in the boiler system and the critical part in the boiler system can be describing through the software. To improve the reliability of the system, some scenario for maintenance strategy was creating. The basic criteria results showed that the critical components in the boiler system were high temperature superheater, pulverizer, IDF, PAF, and Stack. There are two scenarios for creating maintenance strategy, scenario 1 by providing preventive maintenance with a time lag of 3500 hours. scenario 2 by providing inspection measures for t = 50 hours. The results obtained that the best reliability and availability are scenario 2 when compared to existing conditions. However, losses will occur in the form of production loss and cost loss.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Unified Power Flow Controller Placement Effect on Transmission Lines Total Transfer Capability
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The aim of this research is to analyze the Total Transfer Capability (TTC) caused by the Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) installation. The simulation is conducted by implementing the Continuation Power Flow (CPF) method on IEEE-14 Bus System. The simulation results show that the UPFC placement which is carried out by considering bus voltage stability on PV-curve can be used to increase the value of transmission line TTC. As a result, the UPFC is best located to the line which connects to the bus voltage which has the nearest value to the maximum voltage drop constraint when the system is maximally loaded. As a result, the UPFC placement according to scenario 3 (3.3035 p.u.) and 4 (3.3017 p.u.) are the best location to increase the TTC value. This research is expected to be used as a justification for UPFC placement in the real transmission lines system.

articleTitle: Design And Development Of Hardware-Agnostic Solar PV Automated Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Various industrial companies, both engaged in the retail sector as well as services in the business of generation, have utilized information technology to produce information that will be used as a basis in making important decisions. PT. Pembangkitan Jawa Bali (PJB) is one of Indonesia's power generation companies that owns the largest solar power plant in Java Island with a capacity of 1 MW as research and enrichment in the field of new and renewable energy and aims to manage large-scale Solar PV power plant in Indonesia which one of the research scope conducted in Cirata PV Plant is implementing IT technology on the system of monitoring the condition and real time energy production. The system works for combine data from various types and brands of loggers and inverters, process raw data from loggers systematically that can be processed using an application program, perform real time remote monitoring operational conditions, automate production reporting and alerts and report automation. This system can facilitate the process of data acquisition becomes faster and accurate so as to ensure reliable operating conditions, condition monitoring can improve the reliability and availability of the system and reduce downtime.

articleTitle: Numerical Study of the Characteristics of Flow and Heat Transfer Design of USC 1000 MW Superheater Boiler
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Indonesian electricity demand increase average 8.3 % every year, from 236 TWh in 2017 to 480 TWh in 2026, this causes the state-owned electricity generation company looking for efficient, reliable, economical and clean power plant. therefor various Steam Power Plants (PLTU), and other power plants are built with the latest technology as part of the national strategic program of 35,000 MW by the Indonesian government. The construction of a USC power plant in western Java can also overcome power unbalances that could potentially result in blackout electrical power in the electricity Java grid system. The state-owned electricity generation company is managing a project for the construction of the PLTU USC 2 x 1000 MW in Banten, so the authors need to observe the flue gas flow characteristics and heat transfer process of the boiler with the latest technology. Steam Generators with the latest technology of this kind will be increasingly developed in Indonesia and other countries in the future. The boiler data generally refers to the feasibility study, bidding document and documents related to the PLTU that is currently in a construction project, this thesis uses a numerical approach to Computational Fluid Dynamic (CFD) to obtain the characteristics of flue gas flow and heat transfer from flue gas to the boiler tube on the superheater and modeling the heat transfer process from the flue gas to the tube boiler and the distribution of the regulation in various conditions that will be used as a reference evaluating the boiler detail design Ultra Super Critical Coal Fired Power Plant (USC CFPP) , This research results obtained the highest temperature in the superheater tube 1 is at angle of 30° on tube 4 and the lowest on tube 5 at angle 120°. flue gas velocity at the inlet around the superheater 1 tube lower than at the outlet side the inlet side velocity is higher than the outlet side, due to the nose boiler.

Author Keywords: Ultra Super Critical Coal Fired Power Plant

articleTitle: Construction of Waste-to-Energy (WTE) Power Plant in Balikpapan to Handle Waste and Marine Litter Treatment in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Indonesia is the country with the fourth-largest population in the world, with approximately 267 million people in 2019. With a large number of populations, it produced a massive amount of waste. Waste generated in Indonesia reached 175,000 tons per day or 64 million tons of waste annually. The marine litter data in Indonesia is also quite astonishing, as an archipelagic country it turns out that marine plastic waste circulating in our waters is 187.2 million tons. Jenna Jambeck's research in 2015 states that Indonesia is the second-largest producer of marine litter in the world. Meanwhile, in the USA, with a population of approximately 322 million people, chooses to use waste as energy resources. There are 84 WTE facilities over 23 states that can process more than 96,000 tons of waste per day with a baseload electric capacity of 2,679 megawatt-hours. Regarding the waste treatment in the USA that makes it as an energy source, there is also a massive potential for utilizing waste in Indonesia to build WTE plants and facilities. One place that can be considered to built WTE plants in Indonesia is Balikpapan, East Kalimantan. Balikpapan as a big city in the middle of Indonesia and located on the seafront is very suitable as a WTE Plants location because it can cover waste from various locations, both from within Borneo itself and from other islands, especially central Indonesia and eastern Indonesia, and even the marine waste that already circulating in our sea waters.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis on the Effect of Thread Modification on Air Nozzle for CFB Boiler in Pltu Barru
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Uniform air distribution inside furnace is one of the key points to achieve higher boiler efficiency. However, the occurrence of clogging and deformation on air nozzle orifice can affect whole air distribution inside furnace. Existing air nozzle model has 8 orifice holes and attached to windbox using 10 mm long thread. During latest boiler inspection at 2018, about 178 among 1176 air nozzles inside furnace were loose and deformed. Furthermore, there were several occasions during 2018 until 2019 whether unit had to be shutted down due to low windbox pressure because of there were detached air nozzles. This simulation was conducted to analyze the effect of modification in air nozzle design with 5 mm longer threaded connection against various clogging condition. As the result, with 5 mm longer thread connection, there was an increase of life time from averagely 3100 hours operation to 4500 hours under clogged condition. The result give us a huge understanding, by using new air nozzle design we can minimize chance of powerplant to be shutted down due to detached air nozzle before next scheduled outage.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Energy Management Concept in High Rise Office Building (Case Study in SSS Building Jakarta)
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Energy Management Concept as part of Green Building Concept is focused to Improve Energy Efficiency Index (EEI) and Water Consumption Index (WCI). The purpose of this study was to determine how extent the implementation of green building principles in Office Buildings. The results show that the implementation of the Energy Management Concept could also made energy performance more efficient. After Implementing through Retrofitting of the Chiller System, Recycle Waste Water, Replacement of Conventional lamp to Energy Saving LED, and also Conduct Training as well as workshop to all employees and tenants so we can get the optimization of energy saving as well as the saving cost. Based on the comparing data before and after the implementation of Energy Management Concept, it is found that Energy Efficiency Index (EEI) decreased from 238.8 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/year to 134,04 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/year and the Water Consumption Index (WCI) from 50 liter/person/day to 27.18 Liter/person/day, the saving cost from electricity bill payments is IDR. 466,803,325.67/ month (18%) and roughly will Break Event Point (BEP) for 3.86 years, effectively.

articleTitle: Modeling the Temperature of the Distribution Transformer Oil Using Transformer Body Temperature and Power Quality Parameters Based on Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Existing distribution transformers that supply electricity to customers are generally not equipped with temperature sensors. This causes these transformers to be prone to damages due to an extreme increase in their temperature. Such condition could be ameliorated by placing temperature sensor inside each transformer which is unfortunately not physically realizable. Hence, an alternate method is needed to perform the temperature monitoring function. This paper presents a proposed temperature sensor using an electronic device that models the internal temperature of a transformer without installing temperature sensor inside the transformer. The electronic device performs the temperature sensing function by modeling the temperature using Artificial Neural Network (ANN) in conjunction with measured power quality parameters on the secondary side of the transformer and the temperature on the outside of the transformer as measured by infrared sensors. Hardware implementation using the ARM STM32F4 embedded controller demonstrates the ability of the proposed device in producing accurate Intelligent Electronic Device (IED) which can further be developed to provide early online notification when a disturbance occurs.
