articleTitle: The Literature Study of Implementation New Postpaid Energy Meter System for Achieving Operational Cost Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: reducing operation cost in PLN UID Jateng DIY as a part of Indonesia State Electricity Company (PLN) was a great issue by efficiency and maximizing electric selling. The big change reducing operating cost in Distribution Electric Company was by reduced billing cost for postpaid customer. This new methodology of postpaid meter system was called PASTI energy meters used encrypted code for billing and activation meter. This code was use for communication and billing process. This system could reduce operating expenditure because of meter reader operators and disconnection officers not required as indicated postpaid meter energy system conventional previously. The results of the literature study, by implementation 200.000 PASTI energy meters could reduce labor work cost average 2% yearly. It's means cost saving achieved 40 Billion for 5th year ahead.

articleTitle: The Effect of Aging on Microstructure, Mechanical Properties, and Electrical Conductivity of 6061 Aluminium Alloy for Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Aluminium alloy (Al) 6061 become one of the most significant electrical components due to its conductivity performance. House moving contact resistor of circuit breaker in power system is one of the application of this alloy. However, in the manufacturing process, Al 6061 often fails meet the mechanical property and conductivity requirements. The properties of Al 6061 can be improved by treating the alloy with heat to facilitate natural aging or artificial aging. In order to provide data and evaluate the effect of heat treatment, specimens were observed through different holding time and quench media in this research. Specimens were heated to 536<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C in a muffle furnace in order to surpass the solidus line and undergo a single phase. To conduct fast cooling after heating and holding it for some time, water was used to perform quenching. The holding temperature of tempering after solution treatment was maintained by putting specimens in room temperature for 1, 2, and 3 months to age naturally. As a comparison, other specimens were heated in a furnace and held for 15, 18 and 21 hours to allow artificial aging. The results confirmed the important role of heat treatment in microstructure and properties. The formation of Mg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Si precipitates was found which increased tensile strength, hardness, and conductivity. The formation of Mg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Si was influenced by the holding time in the aging process. The longer aging time, the bigger the precipitates.

articleTitle: Special Protection System with Macro VBA-based Descending Method at PT PLN (Persero) South and Central Kalimantan
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Special protection system is a load shedding system that dynamically protects the electricity system from total outages. The special protection system used by PT.PLN (Persero) South and Central Kalimantan is an automatic protection system that is able to protect the internal or external disturbance power system that losses power supply suddenly causing separate subsystems from the interconnection grid, releasing loads quickly using GOOSEs communication IEC61850 between IEDs of several substations by connecting the subsystems from the status circuit breaker conditions in each transmission segment.

articleTitle: Implementation of Fault Current Limiter in West Java 150 KV Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Fault current limiter (FCL) is a novel approach in protecting equipment from excessive fault current. In this paper, the whole implementation process of FCL devices is presented. There are two families of modern FCL technology, namely superconducting FCL (SFCL) and pre-saturated core FCL (PCFCL), each with its own techno-economic characteristics. The advantages and disadvantages of each technology will be explored and be compared with the conventional current limiting device, i.e. series reactor. Sizing and calculation processes, as well as design criteria of each equipment, will be presented. We hypothesized that series reactor as the cheapest current-limiter device would be able to mitigate the fault current problem while maintaining the system’s reliability and efficiency. This hypothesis is based on our observation that in West Java 150 kV system, large fault current flows through bus-tie. On the other hand, no significant current flow through bus-tie was observed in normal condition. Lastly, we present the challenges and lessons learned in implementing FCL from a design project executed together by PLN Enjiniring and PLN TJBB in West Java 150 kV transmission network.

articleTitle: The characteristic of Thermoelectric Energy Generator module installed at the wall of the prime stove
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Thermoelectric Energy Generator (TEG) was used for harvesting thermal energy in stove for electricity generating. TEG was used TEC1-12706 and SP1848-27145SA types. The objective of this research was compared TEG type on electric power generated. TEG module with SP 1848-27145SA type generated electric power more than TEG module TEC1- 12706 type. Electric power generated with TEG following quadratic equation.

articleTitle: Inverter Position Placement Method In PV Farm Using the String PV Cluster on Normal/Partial Shaded Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) Farm is one of the effective way to produce high scaled electrical energy from sunlight. Many research has been done, is powered optimization method on PV Farm generator string cluster base. But, this method needed a bigger inverter power capacity about 240% from it was before. So this research offer a joint powered optimization method on PV Farm generator string cluster base also can reduce the needs of inverter power capacity. Reducing the needs on inverter capacity can be engineered through inverter position by using Smart Control Algorithm(SCA). This research used a PV Farm with 150 kWp capacity, 50 PV string, every string is consist of 12 module. When it got the shading effect then PV string grouped them into three cluster. The cluster criteria is base on voltage difference between string is more than 20%. Next those three output cluster connect to 3 inverter through switch matrix, where the power capacity comes to the three inverter continously are 75%, 20%, and 5% of power capacity in PV Farm. Inverter position controlled is determined SCA. its controller function to raise the ON/Off signal switch on switch matrix series. Process on raising the ON/Off by SCA base on the voltage input and string current PV Farm. The Voltage and electrical current value is captured through electrical sensor reading and voltage sensor on each cluster. With the controller, power of PV Farm could be channel by inverter with a minimize power capacity on the inverter. Base on simulation result , this method could pressure the need of inverter capacity on PV Farm generator cluster base about 140% (has the same power capacity as generator). So it's concluded that this method could work better on optimizing the power and reducing the inverter capacity in PV Farm generator cluster base on normal/partial shading radiation

articleTitle: Market Survey on the Addition of Cilegon Fuel Gas Compression Capacity as the Sourcing Best Practice of EPC Small Scale Project
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Small EPC project will not be economical if the owner use the same approach in developing project design or planning documents as if it is large scale EPC project. The development of procurement planning documents such as feasibility study, term of references and bidding documents in large scale EPC project usually will be supported by at least one international consultancy firm. This is to ensure the quality of the procurement planning documents. It can cost the owner up to several hundred thousand U.S. dollars per document, but it only have small amount of percentage compared to the total project cost. In small EPC project, this cost will have much bigger percentage. The method proposed to develop procurement planning documents for small EPC project is by doing market survey or market sounding mechanism. This method is similar to pre-qualification of bidders but it is emphasized more on technical and financial matters than administrative qualification. In this study, we hypothesize that the project chosen as the best solution will be found among several project alternatives, and we use financial indicator analysis method to test this hypothesis. A case study on how this method implemented can be seen at fuel gas compression capacity addition project in Cilegon combined cycle gas turbine, Indonesia. This method is successfully helping the plant management to develop procurement planning documents independently. This method is also useful to build an analysis of which project financing is more preferable. Market survey on the project provides data which helps owner to determine whether using direct investment or build-own-operate (BOO) or build-operate-transfer (BOT) to finance the project. In the case of the Cilegon compressor project, it was found that BOO project financing was the best project solution that provided the highest IRR of 11.9%.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Tip Designs in Reducing Fire Risk at Cold Vent Stack
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: High cloud voltage during bad weather is one of fire risk factor at cold vent stack with flowing gas inside. This is because of high electrical energy at cold vent stack tip during bad weather compared to minimum ignition energy (MIE) of the gas inside the vent stack. In order to reduce the fire risk, design modification of cold vent stack tip is proposed. This study discusses the electric field distribution at cold vent stack tips with various tip types. COMSOL Multiphysics® software is used to model and simulate three types of cold vent stack tip, including normal, ring and toroidal. Laboratory experiment to validate the simulation has also been conducted with laboratory-scale cloud voltage up to -100 kV. Simulation results show electrical breakdown at normal cloud vent stack tip occur at lower cloud voltage compared to ring and toroidal cold vent stack tip. The simulation result is verified by the laboratory experiment result. As a conclusion, cold vent stack with toroidal tip design is more effective in reducing fire risk compared to normal and ring tip designs.

articleTitle: The Design of Kalimantan Transmission System Interconnection in Electrical Stability Perspective
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: As of the main island in Indonesia, Kalimantan faces a huge challenge in term of electrical system expansion. The distributed load and remote energy source are the main issues that must be highlighted during designing the transmission system. In addition to this challenge, the Indonesia government willing to increase the renewable energy mix. This willingness means to optimize the whole system based on a large hydropower potential. An interconnected transmission system is able to facilitate solutions for answering all those challenges. However, the electrical stability study is required to ensuring that a disturbance in the transmission system does not lead to a major blackout. Furthermore, the maximum clearing time of a fault might be determined from the stability analysis. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the stability study regarding The Kalimantan transmission system design. The study is based on a transient and small-signal evaluation to ensure system stability and resiliency. The presented investigation and insight might be helpful not only for The Kalimantan case but also any large system utility to leverage the transmission system in an enhanced way.

articleTitle: Effect of Sodium Chloride Solution Concentration on Hydrogen Gas Production in Water Electrolyzer Prototype
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Energy is an essential component of human life because all human activities require energy. The current consumed energy comes from fossil fuels that are not renewable in a short time; therefore, they are decreasing over time. The current research shows the possibility of producing energy source from water in which Indonesia as an archipelago country has an abundant source of water. Therefore, Indonesia has a high possibility of developing renewable energy sourced from water. The process of getting hydrogen from water is called the electrolysis process of water. In this study, a water electrolyzer prototype was designed, and an experiment in producing hydrogen was conducted. The water used in this study is 6 liters with a variable that changes the concentration of sodium chloride solution (NaCl) starting from 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50%. The optimal production of hydrogen gas is at the concentration of 50% NaCl solution with the amount of gas produced at 11.29 liters and the mol percent of hydrogen in the product which is 78.45%.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Risk Identification in Oil and Gas Industry
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: There are many methods for risk identification (e.g. scenario analysis, cause-and-effect analysis, and human reliability analysis). Identification with this method has a defect in accuracy and need a longer time to get the results. A new method for electromagnetic risk identification must be developed to be more effective. To identification, risk needs to review a document, measured electromagnetic field site, simulation electromagnetic field, and computerized electromagnetic field identification. This study conducted in 8 plants. There are two measurements. Low and medium frequency measurement, medium and frequency measurement. The most dominant electric field is at the frequency of 8 GHz - 9 GHz with 16 measurement points in the danger category. This method is proven to be effective, with high accuracy and needs short times.

articleTitle: De-aerator Exhaust Waste Heat Recovery Using TEG
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Coal fired-power plant has waste heat from exhaust de-aerator. Changes in coal-fired steam power plant operation cause change in deaerator temperature. The operating of coal-fired steam power plant about 150-300MW. Exhaust de-aerator temperature about 145°-170°C. The thermal energy can be recovered as electricity by using TEG. TEG is thermoelectric generator, an equipment which can convert heat flux to electric energy. TEG convert heat different between hot side and cold side. Dimension 1 Module of TEG is only 56x56x4 mm. The difference deaerator temperature influence TEG's performance. TEG highest voltage and power output is 2.48V and 5.1W obtained. Developing cooling system and MPPT is needed to maximize TEG performance.

articleTitle: Price Demand Elasticity and Potential Saving of Electric Subsidies: Empirical Evidence of Household Socio-Economic Survey
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The analysis of the potential saving of electric subsidies uses hypothetical assumptions about the removal of subsidies for some of a household with connections 900 VA. The National Socioeconomic Survey (SUSENAS) of March 2017 has been used to analyze the price demand elasticity and the potential saving of electric subsidies. Price demand elasticity was obtained using multiple regression model. The results show that households with an installed capacity of 900 VA are most affected by changes in electricity prices compared to other installed power households. However, the characteristics of the total expenditure are similar to non-subsidized households, namely household with an installed capacity of 1300 VA. Given that 95% of the installed 900 VA households are above the poverty line and still enjoy subsidies, the revocation of subsidies through tariff rationalization will save electricity subsidies of Rp. 29.25 trillion per year. Before the tariff rationalization is performed, the government should conduct field verification on households that receive subsidies to improve the effectiveness of the targeted subsidy policy.

Author Keywords: poverty Theme of conference: Energy Public Policy JEL Classification: D12

articleTitle: Hybrid Energy For Remote Islands From Peoples Independent Power Producers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The main challenge of producing electrical energy in Remote areas is, the sources of energy. The inefficient diesel power plant with huge costs of production is still the widely used alternative to meet the energy demand in Remote Area. In some areas PLN only able to supply 6-hour electricity every day with 220 Volt Grid. One of the solution to reduce cost of production and capability to supply 24-hours electricity is using Renewable Energy, The feasible solution to solve this problem is to accommodate energy from privately managed power producers that can produce energy with a Smart Grid. PLN buys their electrical power according to the specific regulations (the lower price than basic electricity tariff, certain percentage of energy which can be bought from independent energy generator, a specific brand for energy generators) and PLN could sell the energy depending on renewable energy capacity installed and the use of a tool named switcher. Its main purpose is to limit the amount of energy that the customers can consume. It can switch the availability of electricity at night using Diesel Power Plant, renewable energy during the day and using battery to smooth and switch the system when there is intermittence. Thus, despite limited power generation, energy supplies are sufficient during the day time, Renewable energy itself reduce system cost of production and low capital for PLN because due to usage of Peoples IPP.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Toothed Log Periodic Antenna as Partial Discharge Sensor in Power Apparatus
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Insulation system is one of the most critical parts in electrical equipment, where it often becomes the factor to electrical failures. Therefore, in order to learn the condition of an electrical equipment, it can be simply monitored by its insulation system condition. Partial discharge (PD) detection is one of the monitoring methods in an insulation system. PD can occur in an insulation material when it is exposed to a high electric field. This paper discusses the design and analysis of toothed log periodic antenna as the sensor for PD detection in power apparatus. This particular antenna is designed and simulated using antenna design software, fabricated on a PCB with FR4 epoxy substrate and with 1.6 mm thickness, and tested using Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) to get the antenna characteristic, as well as tested for PD detection in HV Laboratory that takes PD source from a needle electrode. There are two toothed log periodic antennas that are designed in this research. One of the toothed log periodic antennas has 13.17 dB return loss at 650 MHz, 50 MHz bandwidth, and VSWR of 3.29, and another one has -14.67 dB return loss at 1.24 GHz, 60 MHz bandwidth, and VSWR of 1.90.

articleTitle: Optimization of Economic Dispatch of 150 kV Sulselrabar System using Lagrange Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: In this study, the Lagrange method was used to solve the Economic Dispatch problem in the 150 kV electrical system in South, Southeast and West Sulawesi (Sulselrabar). The South Sulawesi system consists of several thermal and non thermal plants. For this reason, arrangements are needed to regulate the loading of the power plant, so that the amount of electricity generated in accordance with the needs and production costs is to a minimum. This research will propose the Lagrange method to find an economical composition of plants. The case study used was the peak daytime load. In this economic dispatch, the algorithm will work based on the given objective function, the objective function is the cheapest generation cost. From the optimization results of generation for the case of peak daytime load, using the Lagrange method, it was obtaining the total generation cost is IDR. 117,121,631.08/hour to generate power of 339.4 MW with losses of 25.016 MW. While in the real system the total generation cost is IDR. 127, 881, 773.68/hour to generate power of 393.1 MW with losses of 24.956 MW. The Lagrange method can reduce the Sulselrabar system generation costs by IDR. 10,760,142.6/hour or 8.41% in peak daytime loads.

articleTitle: Automation of Electricity System PLN UPDL Banjarbaru Using Passive Infrared Sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Electricity usage not optimal yet in our educational company. Manually button power is a kinda factor that affects electricity usage while it is not used. This situation, using a passive infrared sensor is a big deal to optimizing electricity usage. Passive Infrared Sensor detects the existence of humans in a room by the infrared waves released from the body. That infrared wave is processed by an electronic amplifier to become an action to switch ON/OFF the electricity usage. This PIR installment reduces electricity usage in our room while necessary. The implementation of these tools reduces electricity payment by 25% - 30%, about 12 Milion Rupiah per month.

articleTitle: Reducing the Cogging Torque of Integral Slot Number in Inset-Permanent Magnet Generator
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Permanent magnet generator is kind of electrical machine widely used in our daily life nowadays. This paper, dealt with the optimal design to reduce the cogging torque reduction of permanent magnet generator. For the purposed of study, the integral slot number of 48 slots/6 poles with radial magnetization have been selected. The magnetic flux distribution at the air gap and core of any electrical machine was analyzed and presented in the paper. The cogging and ripple torque is the most issues in permanent magnet generator design. The cogging torque is influenced by the magnetic flux distribution in air gap. To reduce cogging torque, is one of difficult task, since it is influenced by many factors in both the stage of design and stage of manufacturing. In the stage of design, the cogging torque has been exist caused by effect of material used in the machine structure. This paper dealt with cogging torque reduction at the stage of design by applying notching in the magnet edge of the permanent magnet generator. The finite element analysis has been used to compute the permanent magnet generator performance. Using the finite element of FEMM, it was found that the cogging and torque ripple could be reduced effectively compared with the initial structure. They could be reduced as much as 98.8 % compared with the initial structure.

articleTitle: Indonesia Opportunity To Accelerate Energy Transition
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: In the energy sector, Indonesia had responsible for contributing 1.41% of CO2 emissions in the world as well as being the largest emitter in the ASEAN region at 454.9 MtCO2 in 2016 (IEA, 2018). This figure has increased by around 0.1% compared to the previous year, and of course this is not in line with the contents of the Paris Agreement which has concern to emission reduction. Sequentially, sectors that have big impact on carbon emissions are main activity electricity & heat production (37.5%), manufacturing industries & construction (32.8%), transportation (16.4%), and other sectors (13.2%), (KLHK, 2017).

articleTitle: Excessive Water Content Identifying Approach Using Sweep Frequency Response Analysist and Electrical Individual Test for Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Transformer insulation is very influential for keeping the transformer under a good condition during operation. There are several methods to evaluate the insulation condition of power transformer. Sweep Frequency Response Analysist (SFRA), electrical individual test of power transformer such as DC Resistant, Turn Ratio, DC Insulation, Breakdown Voltage, Water Content, and Dielectric Dissipation factor are important methods to seek the failure condition of power transformer. Commonly SFRA is used for evaluating any major failure related with major deformation of winding structure, core and mechanic part of power transformer, but recent studies reveal that SFRA data can be influenced by transformer insulation parameters. Excessive water content inside the transformer will also be evaluated with SFRA band analysist to determine the location. The visual observation will show that the excessive moisture was blended with transformer oil inside and even forming a sludge. This observation provides best practice data to support the previous research about moisture ingress contamination that can act as capacitance to influence the amplitude on SFRA analysist. This research also evaluates several methods that can be used to evaluate water contamination inside power transformer such as DDF and DC Insulation.

articleTitle: The Development of 35 GW Power Generation for Sustainability of PJB Existing Power Plant: An Assessment and Analysis on Java-Bali System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The ambitious 35 GW of mega project on the development of power generation by the government of Indonesia are targeted to be completed by 2019. This mega project was planned to meet the growth of electricity demand by setting the government ambitious goal of achieving of 7 (seven) percent annual economic growth. Notwithstanding the fact, the growth of electricity demand has currently declined due the slowdown of the country economic growth, which only achieve upward of 5 (five) percent by the year of 2016 and 2017. By referring to lower economic growth, there will be less energy required and the country is nowadays facing oversupply of electricity energy. At current development rate, for Java-Bali region is currently having the electricity supply up to 30,000 MW, by leaving a surplus of power about 8,000 MW. Yet, the electricity demand growth in the region is also considered positive every year. Therefore, a comprehensive study has been conducted by using two approach methods, namely plant selection and development selection in order to optimize the sustainability development of PJB Existing Units in Java-Bali System.

articleTitle: Impact of Sizing and Placement on Energy Storage System in Generation Scheduling Considering Transmission Losses
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The existence energy storage system (ESS) can reduce some of the problems in the power system. The problems occur in dispatch, stability, and economical at generation and transmission. ESS is one of a solution to overcome issues about intermittency, load shifting, frequency regulation, energy arbitrage, reserve power support, etc. Impact of size and location of ESS give a significant benefit to the power system. The objective of this paper is to investigate proper sizing and placement of ESS considering the transmission losses. The condition of transmission losses can influence power scheduling on Unit commitment (UC) and reliability system. Thus, an important technique for considering certain ESS is needed. The optimization of the ESS operation is solved using mix integer quadratic programming (MIQP). The result of the optimization is used as input for UC to optimize cost for scheduling generations. The next step is using the UC output to perform power flow analysis for evaluating transmission losses. The total operational cost 24 hours without ESS up to $136.23, ESS installed 100 MWh up to $135.47, ESS installed 60 MWh up to $135.7, and ESS installed 40 MWh up to $135.74. While the result of total losses without ESS reaches 217.636 MW and ESS installed reaches 212.187 MW at bus 6. If ESS installed at bus 19, the losses increase to 220.729 MW. Therefore, the difference in ESS capacity has an impact on system operation, while the placement of ESS yields different losses. The next step of developed optimization needs to be determined ESS of proper location and sizing capacity as part of systems using the best methods metaheuristic to complete the best results.

articleTitle: Smart Grid Technology for Energy Conservation in Street Lights: Lesson Learnt from Six Years’ Operation in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The current problem of most existing street lighting is that their illuminance level is fixed regardless changes on pedestrian flows and passing traffic. Adjusting the illuminance level to actual needs of lightings that varies overnight potentially reduces energy consumptions. Such adaptive systems require a smart street lighting (SSL) technology that is able to monitor and automatically control street lightings in real time. Several cities in Indonesia has used SSL since 2012 and, therefore, this study aims to explore potential SSL expansions in the country. This paper uses a systematic review approach to analyze basic features of SSL technology; SSL global market prospects; factors influencing municipalities' acceptance, and evaluations of SSL systems in Indonesia from 2012 to 2018. Based on the review, policy recommendations are then proposed for the sustainable expansions and operations of SSL systems in Indonesia. One of the recommendations is to enhance the cooperation of energy service companies (ESCOs) to solve financing and technical problems faced by municipalities.

articleTitle: Visibility study of Optimized Hybrid Energy System Implementation on Indonesia’s Telecommunication Base Station
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: The usage of renewable energy in Indonesia’s industrial must be done faster in order to meet the national target of renewable energy usage, but until now the implementation has not been as expected. Especially for the telecommunication industry where 60% of its expenditure is the cost of energy, the implementation of green telecommunication is very helpful in making efficiency while making efforts to protect the environment. On this paper, authors will analyze several constrain for Indonesia’s telecommunication operators in implementing the hybrid energy system as a source of electrification throughout their entire BTS network. The hybrid referred to in this paper is the addition of the on-grid solar panels and also optimized by adding wind turbines to areas that have proper wind speeds to existing sources of electrification. Furthermore, the role of government will also be analyzed in-depth, because without it, the conversion process to renewable energy will not succeed. Design, calculation, and sizing for the optimized hybrid energy system is the major part of this study. Hopefully, this study can find the optimized balance between an investment that operators must spend and government incentives or subsidy, so the cost of electricity for this implementation will be reasonable and profitable for the operators.

articleTitle: Electricity Demand Forecasting Using a Simple-E Expanded Approach at PT PLN (Persero) of Kotamobagu Area From 2018 to 2022
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: National electricity demand has always been increasing every year, the same as the growth of the population along with industrial and technological development. To fulfill that condition, PT PLN (Persero) will compose the electricity system planning for a long period (ten years). That will state into the RUPTL (Electricity Supply Business Plan) Document that verified by The Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources of the Republic of Indonesia. Before the project of electricity system infrastructure begins, then we need to know the electricity demand forecasting in the future that is suitable to be implemented in electrical energy infrastructure since it fulfills the effective and economic feasibility aspects. In this research, we observe PT PLN (Persero) Kotamobagu Area with the data from 2018 to 2022 using a Simple-E Expanded Approach. It is a process of estimation that uses regression models and forecasting simulation from an econometric simulation tool. The results show the total electrical energy needs at PT. PLN (Persero) Kotamobagu Area, for the Year Period above, will continue to increase in the amount of 321.2 GWh, and peak loads up to 61 MW in 2022.

articleTitle: New and Renewable Catalyst Based on Electro-Activated Carbon for Hydrogen Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Understanding of the interaction between adsorbants and metal (aluminium) surfaces have led to descriptors for new and renewable catalyst which have a major impact on the design of heterogen catalysts. On hydrogen production based hydrolysis these understandings still lack. It is considered that the necessity of energy fulfillment could be benefited by using the utilization of hydrogen as a new and green energy source. However, the hydrogen production remains a challenge because its complex reaction and unstable production. We propose here a strategy to overcome this challenge using heterogeneous carbon catalyst derived from coconut shell waste to enhance the stability of hydrogen production through the reaction between water and aluminum metal waste on the support of electro-activated carbon (EAC). We show that EAC could enhance the specific surface area to 394.46 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/g with the average pore diameter of 21.9 Å. The implications of the utilization of EAC could enhance the hydrogen production and stabilization. The optimum average hydrogen production rate could reach to 9.19 mL/min/gr. The conclusion is that the EAC catalyst strategy successfully integrates stabilization and production of hydrogen, opening a route to the low-cost integration of hydrogen production.

articleTitle: Development Of Predictive Maintenance Methodology Utilizing Machine Learning Technology To Support Plant Health Management
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: To maintain availability and reliability in PT. Indonesia Power (IP) power plants at high level, proper maintenance strategy must be well established. IP utilizing Predictive Maintenance (PdM) to predict the equipment conditions from plant healthiness. PdM analyze data trends to predict future behavior of equipment. Recent development in PdM methodology is applying Machine Learning (ML) technology which is proven effective and improves the speed and accuracy in the Plant Health Management (PHM) decision making. The ML technology used utilize anomaly detection based on regressive models. The model utilizes historical data and trains using the linear regression trainer model then predict current value using its lagged past in the time series. The prediction results then evaluated using scoring model. Overall result shows high prediction accuracy indicates in high number from the scoring model. Further analysis performed to forecast equipment condition and prediction of remaining threshold reaching in certain period. The analysis results then fed to database software to be documented and visualized in web-based charts. By employing the analysis provided in the web-based charts, allows engineer to develop appropriate PHM execution strategy. The current development PdM Methodology is proven to be capable of equipment condition prediction by utilizing ML technology. The ongoing development will be aimed in processing more training data with higher granularity and deployment in production environment.

articleTitle: Corporate Strategy Using Strategic Portfolio Analysis in Facing Renewable & Liberalized Electricity Era
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Indonesia's electricity market in the future will be increasingly unfriendly for conventional power plants. The Government through the National Energy General Plan has targeted a mix of variable renewable energy (VRE) reaching 23% by 2025 and dramatically increase its level in the energy sector. Bloomberg also predicts wind and solar will power half the world by 2050 and attracting $ 9.5 billion in new investment between now and then. The electricity market will also tend to be a liberalized market following the trend of electricity in developed countries. PT PJB as an asset owner, asset manager and asset operator of a large portion of conventional power plant in Indonesia will be challenged to deal with these changes. The portfolio owned by PJB is currently supported by the operations and maintenace expertise of conventional power plants. The characteristics of renewable plants that have low operational and maintenance expenditure are a threat to the sustainability of PT PJB in the future. If PJB does not adapt in the current change, PJB will dissapear in the future. This paper proposes a portfolio management strategy to deal with the changes in the electricity market in the long run. In this paper, analysis is carried out using Strategic Portfolio Analysis. At the initial stage, it is necessary to do an internal and external analysis to identify all products and service groups offered by company on the market (product mix) and the current situation on electricity market. Advanced evaluation on the electricity industry is also carried out to get a comprehensive picture of the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats for the company. Critical factors that have been determined then become the basis in preparing specific strategies for asset allocation according to its relative market share and actual or projected sales growth rate.

articleTitle: Placement and Capacity Optimization of Unified Power Flow Controller using Imperialist Competitive Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: This paper offers a consideration to take in implementing a FACTS device to improve the power quality and service reliability provided by power utility companies. The installation of the device must be planned meticulously to get the most benefit from it. A Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) is considered to be used in the 500 kV JAMALI power system in Indonesia. An optimization method based on the Imperialist Competitive Algorithm (ICA) is proposed to find the best location and size of the device. The installation of a common capacitor bank is used as a comparison. The results show that the addition of bank capacitors and UPFC can improve the voltage profile so that the bus voltage can be maintained within the specified value limits (0.95-1.05 p.u.). The use of ICA method for UPFC optimization enabled the reduction of active power losses by 13.92% and the reactive power losses by 14.16%. It is better than the losses reduction obtained on bank capacitors optimization, which was 9.96% of active power losses and 4.28% of reactive power losses.

articleTitle: Design Mini Hydro Power Plant Utilize Discharge Channel Teluk Balikpapan 2x110 MW Coal-fired Steam Power Plant by Finite Element Method Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Technologies and Policies in Electric Power & Energy
abstract: Indonesia's renewable energy has overgrown. The government has a goal of 23 per cent using renewable energy resource to generate electrical power in 2025. In 2019 Indonesia has already utilized 11 per cent renewable energy power or about 6,516.3 megawatts and be going to 23 per cent in 2025. The most popular power plant's type in Indonesia is a coal-fired steam power plant (CFSPP). The portion of CFSPP is about 45.1% of Indonesia's total power plant capacity, and this study informs one of the methods to generate electrical power using renewable energy to achieve renewable energy utilization of Indonesia in 2025. Teluk Balikpapan is CFSPP in East Kalimantan that has two units power plant with a total of 220-megawatt capacity. To renewable energy utilization, discharge channel CFSPP can be modified by installing hydropower plant with small capacity. The existing discharge channel is modified in such a way, like a hydro turbine line addition. The new channel can flow water into a hydro turbine which is the flowrate is up to 40 meter cubic per hour, and the head is about 3 meter. The capacity of hydropower that utilizes the discharge channel of Teluk Balikpapan CFSPP can be found by using a finite element method (FEM) Solidworks software simulation. Teluk Balikpapan discharge channel is observed that maximum electrical power is about 307.86 kilowatt that can supply common auxiliary power consumption. This study is one of the ways to achieve Indonesia's renewable energy utilization in 2025, about 23 per cent.
